newsitem.title: GERMANY: German finance ministry declines comment on ERM.
newsitem.headline: German finance ministry declines comment on ERM.

text.p: The German finance ministry declined to comment on speculation that the European Union's monetary committee would meet at the weekend to discuss the Italian lira's re-entry into the EU exchange rate mechanism.

Italy is eager to re-enter the ERM by the end of the year in order to improve its chances of being among the first tier of EU member states to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999.
A senior source on the sidelines of a the European Banking Congress in Frankfurt told Reuters that Italy had requested a meeting of the monetary committee for Saturday.
"We have no comment on this," a spokeswoman from the Bonn finance ministry said.

The monetary committee has the power to decide on membership of Europe's ERM. Italy crashed out of the ERM in 1992 after its currency had been trading outside of the ERM trading bands. The bands were later widened to ease tensions.
